Understand how it works, down to the binary level.** [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/rea-agents?style=flat-square&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents) [![MCP tool catalog](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-tool_catalog-5c4ee5?style=flat-square)](docs/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog) [![Node.js requirements](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-requirements-339933?style=flat-square&logo=nodedotjs&logoColor=white)](#what-you-can-analyze) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/morluto/rea?style=flat-square)](https://skills.sh/morluto/rea/reverse-engineer-anything) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-f4c430?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1556595354999332884?logo=discord&logoColor=white&label=Discord&color=5865F2)](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) **[Website](https://rea.tools/) · [Guides](https://rea.tools/guides/) · [Showcases](https://rea.tools/showcase/)** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How REA works](#how-rea-works) · [What you can analyze](#what-you-can-analyze) · [Showcases](#showcases) · [Build RL environments](#build-rl-environments) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Documentation](#documentation) npx rea-agents setup
> [!IMPORTANT] > Get REA from [morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea), > [rea.tools](https://rea.tools/), or the [rea-agents npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents). > Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar > repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.




Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. ## Quick start On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron analysis require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks. Recovery steps are in `docs/installation.md` under "Linux owned-process prerequisite". ### Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA entry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry available. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target project. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and [other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See [installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and manual MCP registration and Claude Code/Codex plugin installation. MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` in your MCP registration when you need the complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See "Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide. Complete output schemas are advertised by default. If your client caps the complete `tools/list` frame, set `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact` to bound each advertised output schema, or `off` to omit output schemas entirely. Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and complete structured results. See "Output schemas" in the MCP contracts guide. ### Ask your agent ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. ### Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` `rea --update` is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global output flags. Use `rea update` when combining it with other command controls. Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure and waits for submitted writes to finish. Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`. To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use `bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`. ## How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm. Additional tools and host support depend on the target: | Target | What REA returns | Requirements and guide | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Desktop installations | Runtime candidates, supporting files, component markers and next probes | Built-in bounded directory/header inspection; [desktop applications](docs/desktop-applications.md) | | Native binaries | Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references | Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna; [native analysis](docs/native-investigation.md) | | Offline ELF layout | Sections, segments, original symbols/relocations and static mitigation candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; [binary diagnostics](docs/binary-diagnostics.md) | | Go binaries | Embedded compiler version, modules, replacements and build settings | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; no Go installation required | | GPU code objects | CUDA/HIP targets, selected kernel parameters and resources, retained PTX text | Built-in static ELF/PE/fatbin/CUBIN/PTX inspection; [GPU code objects](docs/gpu-code-objects.md) | | Model artifacts | GGUF / safetensors metadata, tensor declarations and derived totals | Built-in header inspection; optional full-file hash; [model files](docs/model-artifacts.md) | | IL2CPP metadata | Unity global-metadata.dat assembly images, type and method names and index ranges | Built-in static decoding of versions 24, 27, 29, 31 and 39; no Unity required | | Godot PCK | Archive inventory and extraction, original header/directory facts and selected content identities | Built-in static formats 2, 3 and 4; no Godot required | | Rust binaries | Embedded cargo-auditable crate names, versions, sources and dependency edges | Built-in static ELF/PE/thin Mach-O inspection; [Rust binaries](docs/rust-binaries.md) | | PE certificates | Authenticode WIN_CERTIFICATE entries and PKCS#7 signer/X.509 identity fields | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE certificates](docs/pe-certificates.md) | | PE imports | Import and delay-load DLL names, ordinals, IAT RVAs and pefile import hash | Built-in static PE inspection; [PE imports](docs/pe-imports.md) | | ELF notes | PT_NOTE/SHT_NOTE owners, types, GNU build-id and ABI-tag fields | Built-in static ELF inspection; [ELF notes](docs/elf-notes.md) | | Apple IPS crashes | .ips metadata, threads, images, registers and documented crash classes | Built-in static JSON inspection; [Apple IPS](docs/apple-ips.md) | | Linux kernel modules | .modinfo keys, __versions CRCs, this_module presence, and signature trailer | Built-in static ELF inspection; [kernel modules](docs/kernel-modules.md) | | Erlang BEAM | IFF chunks, atoms, exports, imports, lambdas and the Code header | Built-in static BEAM inspection; [Erlang BEAM](docs/erlang-beam.md) | | WASM artifact | Validation, sections, exact import/export WAT forms and decoded WAT | Caller-supplied WABT 1.0.42; `inspect_wasm_artifact` | | EVM bytecode | Dispatch selectors, byte offsets, inferred arguments and mutability | Local raw/hex carrier on Linux x64; [offline EVM guide](docs/evm-bytecode.md) | | SQLite databases | Tables, columns, indexes, views, triggers and selected ordinary-table rows | Local database/WAL snapshot; Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with native SQLite limits | | Recorded Linux crashes | Raw notes, every recorded thread's registers/signals and optional mapping candidates | Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; optional GDB/pwndbg; [recorded crashes](docs/recorded-crashes.md) | | JavaScript / Electron | Modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC and native add-on relationships | Node.js and npm; Linux: procps-compatible `ps`; [application analysis](docs/javascript-application-workflows.md) | | Websites | Page structure, scripts, network observations and requested screenshots | A Chrome-family browser; [browser analysis](docs/browser-observation.md) | | Saved network captures | Requests, responses, exposed payloads and source locations | HAR or Fiddler Everywhere SAZ; mitmdump on Linux for native mitmproxy; [capture guide](docs/web-network-captures.md) | | .NET assemblies | Metadata, CIL instructions, declared native dependencies and build comparisons | None (static only); [managed-code guide](docs/managed-code-analysis.md) | | Android APKs | Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references | Headless JADX and a full JDK on Linux/macOS/Windows x64; [Android guide](docs/android-analysis.md) | | APK signatures | v1/v2/v3/v3.1 signers, certificate fingerprints, key rotation and digest self-consistency | None (static only); `inspect_apk_signature` | | Android devices | Devices, packages, processes, logs, dumps, screen captures, and APK/file transfers | Caller-supplied adb (emulator or hardware); [ADB guide](docs/adb-device-analysis.md) | | JEB projects | Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code | A caller-started JEB client serving MCP, selected with REA_JEB_MCP_URL; [JEB guide](docs/jeb-analysis.md) | | Android resources | Decoded manifest, string tables, locales and version facts | Caller-supplied Apktool launcher; [resource guide](docs/apktool-resource-analysis.md) | | Flutter apps | Dart snapshot hash, per-ABI library digests and engine build provenance | None (static APK parsing); [Flutter guide](docs/flutter-analysis.md) | | Firmware | Regions, extraction results and native-analysis handoffs | Binwalk / Unblob on Linux; [firmware guide](docs/firmware-analysis.md) | | Recorded packets | Selected fields, repeated values, filters and decode-as rules | Linux: TShark 4.x + prlimit; [capture guide](docs/packet-captures.md) | | Packet summaries | Endpoints, DNS, TLS SNI, protocol distribution and HTTP requests | Caller-supplied tshark and capinfos (Linux-verified); [pcap guide](docs/pcap-analysis.md) | | Recorded logic signals | Decoder annotations, sample ranges and diagnostics | Linux: sigrok-cli 0.7.2 + prlimit; [signal recordings](docs/signal-recordings.md) | | Packages and resources | File inventories, digests, plists, Apple bundle anatomy and extracted resources | [Artifact and JavaScript guide](docs/javascript-artifact-reconstruction.md), [Apple applications](docs/apple-application-analysis.md) | | Process behavior | Terminal output, interactions, exit and filesystem observations, and run comparisons | Linux/macOS with a native PTY; [process capture](docs/process-capture.md) | | PyInstaller executables | CArchive members, Python version, entry scripts and extracted bytecode | None (static only); [Python packaged applications](docs/python-packaged-applications.md) | Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running the application. Runtime capture runs or interacts with the selected target using your user permissions; each runtime guide describes its effects. For offline native-binary inspection, REA also supports caller-supplied GNU objdump and Rizin. See the [reverse-engineering tools guide](docs/reverse-engineering-tools.md) for provider setup, CLI commands, and Evidence limitations. REA does not install or update either provider. Native formats and host support vary by provider. See [Hopper and Ghidra setup](docs/installation.md#hopper), the [IDA guide](docs/ida-provider.md) (including an optional native MCP bridge), the [Kuna decompiler guide](docs/kuna-provider.md), and [experimental Windows Ghidra support](docs/windows-ghidra-p0.md). Ghidra also supports [16-bit DOS analysis](docs/ghidra-dos.md). For large binaries, raise the provider's startup deadline with `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` or `REA_HOPPER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`. For provider selection, see the [CLI guide](docs/cli.md#choose-a-provider). Check [release availability](docs/installation.md#released-package-and-main) for features added since the latest npm release. ## Showcases ### DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation Follow a sound call into its position-to-pan helper, inspect the instructions, and turn incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passes 3,205 original-x86 cases and reproduces all 63 compiled function bytes. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/dx-ball/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball) ### Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge Find the renderer's clipboard API, follow it through preload and IPC into the main process, and inspect the rich clipboard format. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/notion/) ### TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation Inspect the original PC-98 game's 16-bit instructions, recover the fixed and aimed angle calculations, and compare the reconstructed C++ with the historical compiler output. [Read the case study](https://rea.tools/showcase/th04/) · [Reconstruction repository](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04) ### Build RL environments with REA Record a web app session, turn its API into tools, and export an environment an AI agent can use. Run it with AgentEnv, then add tasks and reward checks for RL training or evaluation. [Read the guide](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Watch the video](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## Build RL environments Give an AI agent a local environment to practice tasks such as finding an issue or creating a folder, without running the original app. Use it for reinforcement learning (RL) or to test how well an agent completes tasks. REA turns recorded API requests and responses into tools the agent can call. The environment uses the recorded data and supports changes only when the recording confirms their effects. With REA set up in your agent, replace the example URL and folder tasks below with your own: ```text Use REA to build an RL environment from my test web app at http://127.0.0.1:3000. Cover listing, creating, renaming, and deleting folders. You may create and remove test folders. Leave existing data unchanged. Save it in a folder named my-env. Check which operations work and tell me how to run it. ```
Use the command line instead Use these commands if you already have a file containing the app’s recorded browser requests and responses. Running the result also requires AgentEnv and Docker. ```sh rea environment-build ./session.har ./my-env --name my-env --json agent-env run ./my-env ```
REA exports a runnable environment with a basic test to check that it starts and responds. Use it with your RL framework to define task goals, add reward checks, and run training. [Build an environment](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/) · [Environment reference](docs/agent-environments.md) · [Watch the demo on X](https://x.com/reatools/status/2112574822584918075?s=20) ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
## Documentation Start with the website's [worked guides](https://rea.tools/guides/). For exact options, prerequisites and result contracts: - [Installation and setup](docs/installation.md): agent registration, provider configuration, updates and uninstall. - [Readiness and troubleshooting](docs/installation.md#check-readiness-for-your-task): diagnose one agent or analysis engine. - [CLI and Evidence](docs/cli.md): commands, provider selection, snapshots, import/export and exit statuses. - [MCP contracts](docs/mcp-contracts.md) and [agent prompts](docs/mcp-prompts.md): tool results, sessions and guided investigations. - [Tool catalog](docs/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog): generated inventory of tools, providers and CLI commands. - [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md): planned work and capability trackers. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Star history 🎉 **400,000 GitHub stars — thank you!** Thanks to everyone using REA, reporting bugs, requesting features, testing builds, and contributing fixes. ## Disclaimer See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) for responsible-use guidance. The project's position on illegal or unauthorized use covers all REA versions, distribution channels, and platforms; each copy retains its applicable licenses. REA is for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine. ## Contributing We'd love your help with REA! [Open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) to report a bug or suggest a feature, or [send a pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls) to improve the code or docs. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and checks, [testing](docs/testing.md) for verification lanes, and the [architecture map](docs/architecture.mermaid) for selected layers and dependency paths. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) REA-authored code is licensed under MIT. Third-party material retains its own licenses and copyright notices; see [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the dependency inventory, preserved license texts, and external-tool terms. **You must legally obtain and be authorized to use commercial tools**, including IDA Pro / Hex-Rays decompilers, Hopper, and JEB, under their applicable licenses. REA grants no tool license, key, or activation entitlement. Trials and demos remain subject to vendor terms, including user, feature, automation, and output sharing restrictions. Cracked copies, stolen keys, unauthorized key sharing, and bypassing license restrictions are not authorized. This guidance does not amend MIT or third-party licenses.

items.readme_text:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want, or just ask in your own words and Claude picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Catch your agent's mistakes and blind spots before the shit hits the fan.


Quick start • Test your agent • What you get back • Docs • Contributing

## How can you trust your AI agent? How do you know it will do its job the way it's supposed to, respecting your business as a whole: its intentions, its goals and who in the organization may do what? And how do you know it won't do something nobody asked for or authorized? That's why we built iFixAi, the independent auditor for agentic operational alignment and assurance. It puts your agent in a simulation of your business, sends it the requests a real day brings, including the ones that push it past its role, and a judge grades every reply. Every finding shows what was asked and what your agent did. The risk goes beyond cybersecurity, governance or compliance on their own, so iFixAi's inspections combine AI red teaming, governance, assurance and philosophy. ## Quick start See it work in a minute. No API key needed: it runs on a built-in demo agent with canned replies and canned grades, so you see the flow before you connect anything real. For a real audit, iFixAi picks a judge from a different provider than your agent. You need Python 3.10 or newer (a stock Mac's `python3` is 3.9, so check `python3 --version`). In a fresh virtualenv (`python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`): ```bash pip install ifixai ifixai author reference -o reference.yaml ifixai validate reference.yaml ifixai run --provider mock --eval-mode self --fixture reference.yaml ``` This builds the simulation environment for an example agent, a support agent at a fictional fintech ([its profile](ifixai/fixtures/reference/profile.json)), checks it, and runs the [10 default inspections](#what-a-default-run-covers) on the demo agent. The scorecard prints in your terminal and the reports land in `./ifixai-results/`. On Windows, run `py -m venv .venv`, then `.venv\Scripts\activate`. If `ifixai` isn't found, use `python -m ifixai.cli.main`. ## Test your own agent Any agent with a chat endpoint must be audited, and iFixAi can audit it. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint works as it is; anything else takes [a few lines of Python](docs/testing-your-agent.md). Any model can be the judge: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, OpenRouter and more. iFixAi picks one from the keys you've set, never your agent's own provider. There are two ways to run it. ### With your coding agent (recommended) Install the plugin or the skill, then ask your coding agent to *"run iFixAi on my agent"*. It finds your agent, builds its simulation environment, shows the cost before anything is billed, runs the audit and explains what it found. #### Plugin (Claude Code and Codex) In [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), run these, then ask, or type `/ifixai:ifixai` (`/reload-plugins` if it doesn't show up): ``` /plugin marketplace add ifixai-ai/iFixAi /plugin install ifixai@ifixai-community ``` Already installed? Run `/plugin marketplace update ifixai-community`, then `/reload-plugins`, to get the latest. Codex: run these in your terminal, then start Codex and ask. Moving from `ifixai@ifixai-ai`? See [plugin/README.md](plugin/README.md). ``` codex plugin marketplace add ifixai-ai/iFixAi codex plugin add ifixai@ifixai-community ``` #### Skill (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed and more) ```bash uvx ifixai install --agents cursor ``` Then type `/ifixai-skill` in that agent. Swap `cursor` for `claude`, `vscode`, `windsurf`, `cline`, `continue`, `gemini`, `zed` or `all`. More in [get started](docs/get-started.md#run-it-from-your-coding-agent). ### With the guided CLI 1. Describe your agent: copy the [reference profile](ifixai/fixtures/reference/profile.json) to `my-agent.json` and edit it ([how](docs/fixture_authoring.md)). Or let the plugin or skill do it: your coding agent reads your agent's code and writes the profile for you. 2. Build its simulation environment and check it. Install the extra for the judge you'll use: `openai` here, or `anthropic`, `gemini` and so on. ```bash pip install "ifixai[openai]" ifixai author my-agent.json -o my-agent.yaml ifixai validate my-agent.yaml ``` 3. Set up the run with the wizard. It asks for your agent's endpoint, the judge and the suite, finds the judge's key and saves it all to `ifixai.yaml`. Then pass your agent's own token, see the plan before anything is billed, and run: ```bash ifixai setup export AGENT_API_KEY=... # your agent's own token ifixai run --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY" --dry-run ifixai run --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY" ``` `--dry-run` shows how many tests and judge calls the run makes, and any checks that don't apply to your agent and why, then stops. Prefer flags, for scripts or CI? The same run in one command. This example grades with an OpenAI key; for another judge, set that provider's key. ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... export AGENT_API_KEY=... # your agent's own token ifixai run --provider http --endpoint --api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY" --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --dry-run ``` `` is your agent's base URL, up to `/v1`. Use a staging copy, because the probes are real requests. No auth on it? Swap `--api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY"` for `--auth-method none`. ## What you get back - A pass or fail for each inspection, with the evidence behind it. - An A to F grade from five core pillars: fabrication, manipulation, deception, unpredictability and opacity. - Three mandatory minimums (B01, B08 and P01). Failing any of them caps the grade at D. - Reports in JSON and Markdown, so you can compare runs or gate CI with `--min-score`. More on [scoring](docs/scoring.md) and [every inspection](docs/inspections.md). ## What a default run covers `ifixai run` runs these 10 inspections. They're quick, they all work over chat, and together they're enough for a grade. Add `--full-run` for all 61 inspections; any that can't apply to your agent are set aside first, and the run tells you why. | Impact | ID | Checks that your agent… | |---|---|---| | High | `B01` | only lets a role use the tools it is allowed to use · *mandatory minimum* | | High | `B08` | cannot be talked into more access than the user has · *mandatory minimum* | | High | `P01` | never runs a destructive action for someone not allowed to · *mandatory minimum* | | High | `B12` | resists prompt injection | | High | `B09` | spots and blocks requests that break your policies | | High | `B27` | does not hand one user's private data to another | | Medium | `B06` | says when it is unsure instead of guessing with confidence | | Medium | `B16` | reports a failure instead of pretending it worked | | Medium | `B18` | sticks to the task it was given | | Medium | `B20` | follows exact instructions on format, length, and content | Other suites and options: [CLI](docs/cli.md#suite-options). ## Docs - New here: [Get started](docs/get-started.md) - Doing something: [Test your agent](docs/testing-your-agent.md) · [Build a simulation environment](docs/fixture_authoring.md) - Looking it up: [CLI](docs/cli.md) · [Python API](docs/python-api.md) · [Scoring](docs/scoring.md) · [Inspections](docs/inspections.md) - How it works: [Methodology](docs/methodology.md) · [Case studies](case_studies/) - Beyond live runs: [Audit recorded actions](docs/trajectory-assurance.md) · [Policy Lab](docs/business-policy-lab.md) - Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [good first issues](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22). Questions: a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi/issues) or **info@ime.life**. Security: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). License: [Apache 2.0](LICENSE).

# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Google Antigravity. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Antigravity. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)

- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree.

A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on. The agent acts on a ref and snapshots again to check, with no pixel matching; the loop stays in your agent. On macOS, CLI calls reuse a private command host for each snapshot namespace and binary build. It retains native accessibility objects so a removed row cannot silently resolve to a surviving row with the same identifier. The host exits after 15 idle minutes. `TMPDIR` must be owned by the current user with mode `0700`; the standard macOS per-user temporary directory satisfies this requirement. Headless calls still prohibit foreground activation and synthesized input. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. The optional [JEV helper](skills/jev-desktop/SKILL.md) sends screen descriptions to a configured model provider; it is separate from the native CLI. See [privacy and data handling](docs/faq.md#what-data-can-contain-private-information). ## Installation Install on macOS, Windows or Linux with npm: ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop version ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. Official Homebrew and Scoop packages are being submitted; they are not yet available in the default catalogs. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. - **macOS** needs Accessibility permission: `agent-desktop permissions --guide`. - **Windows** needs no grant for apps at your terminal's integrity level. - **Linux** needs the user's graphical session with `at-spi2-core`. See [installation and permissions](docs/install.md) for package-manager behavior, release archives, and building from source. ## Quick start Observe, act on a ref, observe again. Any app name from `agent-desktop list-apps` works; Finder is the macOS example. Each command prints one JSON envelope; a trimmed snapshot follows the commands. ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` ```json { "version": "2.5", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "window": { "id": "w-204749", "title": "Downloads" }, "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions go through the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. ## For AI agents The binary carries its own docs, matched to its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Every command prints one envelope with `ok` and either `data` or `error`. An error carries a `code`, a `disposition` and usually a `suggestion`; retry only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. The contract, error codes and exit codes are in [docs/json-output.md](docs/json-output.md). ## Commands It ships 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | | macOS | Windows | Linux | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Accessibility tree | Yes | Yes | Yes (AT-SPI) | | Click / type / keyboard | Yes | Yes | AT-SPI; X11 / GNOME keys | | Mouse input | Yes | Yes | X11, `--headed` | | Screenshot | Yes | Yes | X11 windows; Wayland portal | | Clipboard | Yes | Yes | Yes; Wayland needs `wl-clipboard` | | App & window management | Yes | Yes | Launch/list; X11 window control | | Notifications | Yes | Yes | GNOME Shell | | Shell surfaces (`open-system-surface`) | Planned | Yes | GNOME tray, Action Center | The Windows surface and `launch` notes and the Linux X11 and Wayland notes are in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md#platform-notes). `agent-desktop skills get platform` prints the full capability table for the OS you run on. ## Language bindings Each release also ships `libagent_desktop_ffi` for macOS, Linux and Windows, so a program can call the tool in process instead of starting the CLI for each command. `agent-desktop skills get ffi` covers the entry points, memory ownership and threading rules. ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(6) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, replace `agent-desktop-macos` in that list with `agent-desktop-windows`; on Linux, with `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. Build from source: [docs/install.md](docs/install.md#from-source). ## Documentation | I want to... | Read | |---|---| | Fix an install problem, grant permissions, verify a download or build from source | [docs/install.md](docs/install.md) | | Parse the JSON envelope, error codes and exit codes | [docs/json-output.md](docs/json-output.md) | | Drive the tool as an AI agent | `agent-desktop skills get desktop` ([skills/agent-desktop/](skills/agent-desktop/)) | | Learn what differs on one OS | [macOS](skills/agent-desktop-macos/), [Windows](skills/agent-desktop-windows/), [Linux](skills/agent-desktop-linux/) | | Call the C library | [skills/agent-desktop-ffi/](skills/agent-desktop-ffi/) | | Look up the vocabulary: refs, snapshots, sessions | [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md) | | Contribute and pass the gates | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | | Read the engineering rules | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | | Learn from past bugs and lessons | [docs/solutions/](docs/solutions/) | | Find answers to common questions | [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md) | | Report a vulnerability | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | | Get help | [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) | ## License Apache-2.0

Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

--- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`. Install with a single command: ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. **Key Features:** - 🧠 **Persistent Memory** - Context survives across sessions - 📊 **Progressive Disclosure** - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility - 🔍 **Smart Search (Default)** - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill - 🖥️ **Local My Work** - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **TeamBrain** - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Claude Desktop Skill** - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations - 🔒 **Privacy Control** - Use `` tags to exclude sensitive content from storage - 🖼️ **Screenshots (opt-in, off by default)** - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/`, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images-opt-in)) - ⚙️ **Context Configuration** - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected - 🤖 **Automatic Operation** - No manual intervention required - 🔗 **Citations** - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview)** - System components & data flow - **[Architecture Evolution](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture-evolution)** - The journey from v3 to v5 - **[Hooks Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture)** - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks - **[Hooks Reference](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/hooks)** - Every hook entry explained - **[Worker Service](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/worker-service)** - HTTP API & Bun management - **[Database](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database)** - SQLite schema & FTS5 search - **[Search Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/search-architecture)** - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database ### Configuration & Development - **[Configuration](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** - Environment variables & settings - **[Development](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** - Building, testing, contributing - **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** - Common issues & solutions --- ## How It Works **Core Components:** 1. **Lifecycle Hooks** - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, `claude-mem hook claude-code `, run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH 2. **Smart Install** - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on `claude --init` / `--maintenance`, plus `npx claude-mem install` / `repair`) 3. **Worker Service** - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun 4. **SQLite Database** - Stores sessions, observations, summaries 5. **mem-search Skill** - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure 6. **Chroma Vector Database** - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details. --- ## MCP Search Tools Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through **4 MCP tools** following a token-efficient **3-layer workflow pattern**: **The 3-Layer Workflow:** 1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result) 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result) **How It Works:** - Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory - Start with `search` to get an index of results - Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations - Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs - **~10x token savings** by filtering before fetching details **Available MCP Tools:** 1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs) **Example Usage:** ```typescript // Step 1: Search for index search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10) // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456) // Step 3: Fetch full details get_observations(ids=[123, 456]) ``` See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples. --- ## System Requirements - **Node.js**: 20.0.0 or higher - **Claude Code**: Latest version with plugin support - **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing) - **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing) - **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled) --- ### Windows Setup Notes If you see an error like: ```powershell npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet ``` Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation. Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks). --- ## Configuration Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings. To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources. See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples. ### Mode & Language Configuration Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting. This option controls both: - The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation) - The language used in generated observations #### How to Configure Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`: ```json { "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh" } ``` Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. To see all available modes locally: ```bash ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/ ``` #### Available Modes | Mode | Description | |------------|-------------------------| | `code` | Default English mode | | `code--zh` | Simplified Chinese mode | | `code--ja` | Japanese mode | Language-specific modes follow the pattern `code--[lang]` where `[lang]` is the ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., `zh` for Chinese, `ja` for Japanese, `es` for Spanish). > Note: `code--zh` (Simplified Chinese) is already built-in — no additional installation or plugin update is required. #### After Changing Mode Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration. --- ## Development See the **[Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow. --- ## Troubleshooting If experiencing issues, describe the problem to Claude and the troubleshoot skill will automatically diagnose and provide fixes. See the **[Troubleshooting Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** for common issues and solutions. --- ## Bug Reports Create comprehensive bug reports with the automated generator: ```bash cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack npm run bug-report ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please: 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch 3. Make your changes with tests 4. Update documentation 5. Submit a Pull Request against `main` Releases ship from `main` and are published to npm. See [Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development) for contribution workflow. --- ## License Claude-Mem is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. We chose Apache-2.0 because durable agentic memory should be easy to embed in developer tools, local agents, MCP servers, enterprise systems, robotics stacks, and production agent harnesses. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for full details. See [docs/license.md](docs/license.md) and [docs/ip-boundary.md](docs/ip-boundary.md) for licensing scope and the open/commercial boundary. **Note on Ragtime**: The `ragtime/` directory is licensed under the **Apache License 2.0**. See [ragtime/LICENSE](ragtime/LICENSE) for details. --- ## Support - **Documentation**: [docs/](docs/) - **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues) - **Repository**: [github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) - **Official X Account**: [@Claude_Memory](https://x.com/Claude_Memory) - **Official Discord**: [Join Discord](https://discord.com/invite/J4wttp9vDu) - **Author**: Alex Newman ([@thedotmack](https://github.com/thedotmack)) --- **Built with Claude Agent SDK** | **Works with Claude Code** | **Made with TypeScript** --- ### What About CMEM? CMEM is a token created by a 3rd party but officially embraced by the creator of Claude-Mem (Alex Newman, @thedotmack). The token acts as a community catalyst for growth and a vehicle for bringing CMEM to the developers and knowledge workers that need it most. items.readme_text:
Mika

简体中文 · [English](README.en.md) **你手机上的私人 AI 助理，替你操作 App、上网、把事办成。**
它在一块看不见的后台屏上干活，你照样刷你的手机。

⬇ 下载 Mika（安卓 APK）

[安装](#安装) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [能做什么](#能做什么) · [常见问题](#常见问题) · [参与贡献](#参与贡献)
## 安装 **方式一：在手机上自己装** 1. 从 [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest) 下载最新的 APK，安装。 2. 打开 Mika 设置里的「设置手机操作」向导，配对一次无线调试（[设置指南](docs/setup-guide.md)）。 3. 在设置里的「模型」添加服务商、填 API Key，或者用 ChatGPT、xAI、OpenRouter 账号登录。 每一步的细节见下文的[快速开始](#快速开始)。 **方式二：让电脑上的 AI 助手帮你装** 手机用数据线连上电脑，在手机上打开 USB 调试（开发者选项里别的开关不要动，除非 AI 助手请你打开；有的会清除手机数据），然后把下面这句话发给电脑上能执行命令的 AI 助手： ``` 请按 https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/install-with-agent.md 的步骤，帮我把 Mika 安装到通过 USB 连着的安卓手机上。 ``` 它会检查手机、下载安装、打开需要的权限，需要你在手机上点的时候会停下来告诉你。API Key 由你自己在 Mika 里填，不经过它。 **装好之后：让电脑上的 AI 工具直接用 Mika（MCP）** 手机用数据线连着电脑，在电脑上运行： ``` adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/connect-computer.sh adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765 ``` 第一条会打开 Mika 的电脑连接，并打印连接信息（地址 `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp` 和令牌）；把它们填进电脑上 AI 工具的 MCP 配置，它就能给 Mika 派任务、查进度、拿结果。手机上不用点；只经数据线连接、要令牌，Wi-Fi 上连不到；付款这类确认只能在手机上点。用方式二安装时，AI 助手会顺手帮你接好。详见[电脑连接说明](docs/mcp.md)。 > **English summary** > > Mika is an Android app that takes a one-sentence request and carries it out on your phone. It drives apps on a private background screen (so you can keep using your phone), browses the web in a built-in desktop-class browser, and runs scripts in a local Linux sandbox. You bring your own model API key (several providers are supported as presets, plus any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or OpenAI Responses endpoint). There is no Mika server: your requests go only to the model provider you configure. > > Status: **public beta**, changing quickly (see [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases) for versions and changes). Chat, web and sandbox tasks work on Android 11+; phone app control needs Android 12+, with Android 14+ recommended. The sandbox runs on arm64 devices only. The app UI is available in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and English (follows your system language; switch in Settings › Language); see the [full English README](README.en.md). Licensed under Apache-2.0. ## Beta 说明 - 这是早期公开测试版，功能和界面还在快速变化，升级时可能有不兼容的改动。 - 目前主要在一台安卓 14 手机上测试过。别的安卓版本、别的手机上可能遇到没见过的问题，欢迎[反馈](#参与贡献)。 - Mika 会替你操作第三方 App 和网站，请先读[免责声明](#免责声明)。 ## 演示


后台发微信：左边是 Mika 的对话页，右边是 Mika 在后台屏上的每一步
（加速 4 倍；聊天列表已打码）


后台翻完微信群，总结今天聊了啥
（加速播放；总结正文涉及群友发言，已打码）
打开小红书，总结一位博主的内容
（加速播放）
在 BOSS 直聘网页上给 3 个岗位打招呼
（加速播放）

打开 Hacker News，读出首页前 5 条和分数
（加速 1.5 倍）
在 Google Flights 上找旧金山到纽约最便宜的直飞
（加速 3 倍；价格按网络所在地区显示为港币）
在 Amazon 上找 30 美元以内、4.5 星以上的 USB-C 充电器，加进购物车，停在结账前
（加速 3.5 倍）

在 BOSS 直聘网页上找岗位、打招呼
打开汽水音乐，看广告领听歌权益
在美团上凑满减、点外卖，付款前问你
## 能做什么 你用一句话交代一件事，Mika 在手机上替你办。 ### 操作任何 App，不占你的屏幕 手机上装的 App 都能操作，不用事先适配：Mika 像人一样看屏幕、找按钮、点击输入，看得到就能操作。 - 在一块单独的后台屏上打开 App、读界面、点击、输入、滚动，你照常用手机；对话页上的小画面实时显示它在做什么。 - 能逐屏读长列表和聊天记录，比如「帮我总结一下某个群今天都聊了些啥」。 - 界面读不出来的 App（自己画界面、控件没有名字）也能用：Mika 用随 APK 自带的文字识别读屏上的字；配了能看图的模型时，还能看图找按钮和输入框。 - 能把一段文字直接分享进某个 App（发消息、记笔记），收件人和发送仍由 Mika 在那一页上点。 - 系统问「用哪个 App 打开」、装了两份的 App 问「打开哪一个」、一个 App 打开另一个 App（比如跳到付款页）时，Mika 认得出来：能处理的接着做，要你选或要你亲手处理的，会停下来请你在屏幕上操作。 - 需要你亲手处理的事（登录、验证码、付款）会发通知请你接管：App 挪到主屏，你处理完交还，Mika 重新核实再继续。 ### 内置浏览器 - 任何网站都能打开：在后台打开网页，用真实的点击和键盘输入操作页面，默认按电脑版网页打开。 - 能读页面正文，也能读页面自己收到的数据；支持下载、上传。 - 登录过的网站保持登录；侧栏「浏览器」里可以自己浏览，在这里登录的网站 Mika 办事时也能直接用。 - 翻页有节奏：同一个网站连着换页会停一停，对限制浏览快慢的网站停得更久；认得出风控拦截页，交给你处理而不是硬闯。 ### 此刻的屏幕 - 你在别的 App 里时，屏幕边上有一颗 Mika 悬浮胶囊，显示后台任务的进展、要你处理的事和结果，点开可以插话、回答、同意或停止。 - **双击胶囊**，把你正在看的这一屏发给 Mika，比如「这个怎么回」「帮我记下来」；也可以在卡片里截屏、补一句话再发。 ### 定时与条件任务 - 「明早 9 点提醒我」「每天早上看看天气，下雨才告诉我」「每周五做某件事」。 - 到点在原对话里执行，结果送回来；定时任务页可以暂停、改时间、立即执行、删除。 ### 随时插话、随时停 - 任务进行中可以继续说话，补充或更正要求，Mika 在下一步之前读到。 - 按停止后，Mika 会补几行交代：做了什么、看到了什么、发出了几次、哪些没做完。下次说「继续」它知道从哪接着做。 ### 询问 / 自主 - 默认是**询问**：只有花钱（下单、付款）先问你，发消息、提交、删除这些都直接做完。也可以换成**自主**，连付款也不先问。详见[下文](#询问--自主模式)。 ### 记忆 - 记住你明确说过的事实、偏好和做事方式（做事方式要你批准），可以查看、修改、删除；只从你自己说的话里记，密码、验证码、卡号这类不记。记忆加密保存在手机上。 ### 熟悉的 App 和网站，做得更快更稳 没有任何说明，Mika 也能看着屏幕把事办成。有些 App 和网站另外写了使用知识（入口在哪、常见做法、要注意什么），Mika 用到时自动查阅，少走弯路。比如进了聊天 App 直接知道怎么找联系人、翻聊天记录；打开招聘网站知道怎么筛岗位、打招呼。另有几类事情的通用做法。知识持续增加，人人可以补充：它们是放在 [`core/src/main/resources/knowledge/`](core/src/main/resources/knowledge/) 和 [`core/src/main/resources/skills/`](core/src/main/resources/skills/) 下的纯文本文件，[欢迎补充](#参与贡献)。 已经写了使用知识的（没写到的 App 和网站照样能用）： | 类别 | 内置 | |---|---| | **App** | Android 设置、百家号、哔哩哔哩、BOSS直聘、Chrome、得到、抖音、飞书、Gmail、即刻、快手、领英、QQ邮箱、Telegram、今日头条、Uber、Uber Eats、微信、微博、WhatsApp、闲鱼、小红书、知乎 | | **网站** | Amazon、哔哩哔哩、Google Calendar、豆瓣、抖音、Instagram、Gmail、Google Maps、Telegram、百度贴吧、微博、搜狗微信、WhatsApp、小红书、小宇宙、YouTube、知乎、BOSS直聘 | | **通用做法**（技能） | 把内容整理成文字、处理 PDF 文档、查清一件事、消息与邮件 | ### 成批的事 - 成批做事（比如逐个打招呼、投递）直接开始，不用先跟你确认名单；每两次之间隔开一段随机时间，做到网站自己说「到上限了」就停下告诉你。 ### 过程可查 - 回答下面列出来源（读过的页面、截图）；每次任务都有可回看的过程记录。 - 每次任务一行小结：总用时、和模型来回几次、用了多少 Token、多久看到第一次反馈；设置里的「Token 用量」按天、按服务商、按模型统计。 ### Linux 沙箱 - 每个对话一个工作区，可以跑 Python、Node 和 shell 命令，处理你发来的文件，把结果存到手机的「下载/Mika」。 - 默认断网，需要时在设置里的「文件与计算环境」打开「允许脚本联网」。只支持 arm64 设备。 ### 电脑上的 AI 工具也能用（CLI / MCP） 手机连着电脑时，电脑上的 AI 工具可以通过 MCP 把任务交给 Mika，在手机上办完把结果拿回去。一条命令打开，只经数据线、要令牌；也可以在设置里打开局域网连接（默认关）。见[电脑连接说明](docs/mcp.md)。 也可以安装[电脑端 CLI 与 Agent Skill](docs/cli.md),用 `mika connect`、`mika task run`、`mika task wait` 完成连接和任务交接。CLI 与 MCP 并列接入同一份手机任务服务,CLI 不需要配置 MCP;需要包含任务 API v1 的 APK。 ## 快速开始 ### 系统要求 | 项目 | 要求 | |---|---| | 安装、聊天、网页与沙箱任务 | 安卓 11 及以上（沙箱仅支持 arm64） | | 操作手机 App | 安卓 12 及以上；安卓 12、13 上后台操作可能影响主屏焦点 | | 推荐 | 安卓 14 及以上：后台屏有自己的焦点，不影响你在主屏打字；不同对话的任务同时进行也需要它 | | Linux 沙箱 | 仅 arm64 设备；其他设备照常安装，沙箱显示「此设备不支持」 | | 模型 | 一个支持工具调用的大模型 API Key | ### 1. 下载安装 从 [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest) 下载最新的 APK 安装。 ### 2. 无障碍（可以先跳过） Mika 靠无障碍读界面、做点按。不用手动去开：下一步配对成功后，Mika 会自己把它打开。从 GitHub 下载安装的 App，手动打开无障碍时常被系统拦下（提示「受限制的设置」），让 Mika 自己开能省掉这个麻烦。向导里到这一步时选「跳过」即可。 ### 3. 配对无线调试（只需一次） 打开设置里的「设置手机操作」向导，照着清单做：打开开发者选项、USB 调试、无线调试，然后用 6 位配对码配对。开发者选项里 Mika 没提到的开关不要动，有的会清除手机数据，比如「以 16KB 页面大小启动设备」。 第一次设置、卡在某一步，或者不知道配对码填在哪里：看[手机操作设置指南](docs/setup-guide.md)，每一步都写了在哪里点、怎么算成功、常见问题怎么办。 为什么要这一步：Mika 有一个内置的手机助手，要在后台屏上启动和操作 App，需要借用安卓自带的无线调试来启动它。全程在手机上完成，不需要电脑和数据线。配对过后，如果无线调试被系统关掉了（换 Wi-Fi、重启手机后安卓会关掉它），Mika 在你允许的前提下会自己把它重新打开。 手边有电脑和数据线的话，也可以不配对：先打开一次 Mika，插着线在电脑上运行 `adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/usb-start.sh` 启动手机助手；但每次重启手机后都要再运行一次。这些也可以交给电脑上的 AI 助手，见[用电脑上的 AI 助手安装](docs/install-with-agent.md)。 只用上网、文件和聊天的话，这一步可以先跳过。 ### 4. 添加模型 打开设置里的「模型」（第一次打开 App 时也会引导你）。 内置 DeepSeek、通义千问、Kimi、智谱、硅基流动、火山方舟、MiniMax、阶跃星辰、腾讯混元、百度千帆、OpenRouter、OpenCode Go、Anthropic、Gemini、OpenAI、xAI、Mistral、Groq、Ollama、LM Studio 等服务商预设；其他服务商选「自定义」，OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic、Gemini、OpenAI Responses 接口都能接。 也可以不填 Key，用账号登录：添加服务商最上面是「用账号登录 · 不用填 Key」一组，点一家先看说明，再去浏览器里登录，登录后回到 Mika，能看到账号、可用的模型，可以直接设为主模型。 - **ChatGPT**（Plus 或 Pro，用你的套餐额度）：点「使用 ChatGPT 继续」，在浏览器里登录。 - **xAI / Grok**（SuperGrok 或 X Premium+ 订阅）：浏览器里打开 xAI 的确认页，核对手机上显示的短码后同意。这项登录借用 xAI 官方命令行工具的公开登录入口，不是 xAI 专门给 Mika 开的，xAI 可能限制这种用法；有的订阅档位登录后仍不能调用（提示 403），那时改用 xAI 的 API Key。 - **OpenRouter**：OpenRouter 官方给第三方应用的授权。同意后 OpenRouter 给 Mika 一把属于你的 Key（名字是 Mika），用量从你的 OpenRouter 余额里扣；不想用了，在 OpenRouter 的 Keys 页面删掉它。 退出登录只清这台手机上的登录信息。 1. 添加服务商：选一个预设，或选「自定义」填接口地址；填 API Key。Ollama、LM Studio 这类自己机器上跑的服务，地址预填了默认端口，改成那台机器的地址即可，Key 可不填。 2. 点「测试并保存」，连上第一家时会自动选一个主模型。 3. 主模型要支持工具调用。可选：看图模型（看懂界面、看图找按钮）、轻量模型（便宜快的即可，处理判断结局、提取记忆等小事）。 用 ChatGPT 登录或 Responses 接口的模型，可在各用途卡片下调整「思考强度」。默认用服务商默认值；选「用主模型」时也跟随它的强度，明确选同一个模型则可分别设置。档位优先采用服务商报告的列表；没报告时提供手动选项，实际支持情况以服务端为准。更高强度通常更慢、消耗更多 token。 ### 5. 试一试 空对话里有几条示例，点一下就能改了再发。也可以这样说： - 「帮我总结一下微信群今天都聊了些啥」 - 「打开小红书，帮我总结一下某个博主最近发的内容」 - 「帮我订明天早上 9:40、9:50、10:00 的闹钟」 - 「每天早上 8 点看看天气，下雨才告诉我」 ## 询问 / 自主模式 全局一个开关：设置里的「开发者选项」→「自主模式」，关着是询问，打开是自主。 | 模式 | 行为 | |---|---| | **询问**（默认） | 只有花钱的那一步先问你：下单、提交订单，或者页面上显示着应付金额时的确认、提交。卡片上写明在哪、买什么、多少钱，只能同意这一次或不同意。付款本身由你亲手完成。发消息、发帖、提交表单、删除、改设置这些都不问，直接做完。 | | **自主** | 连付款也不先问你，直接做完。成批做事时两次之间的间隔照样保留。 | - 换了开关管之后的所有任务；正在做的任务从询问换成自主，下一步起付款也不再问。 - 登录、验证码、付款密码这类要你亲手处理的事，两种模式都会请你接管；信息不够、或者只有你能选（比如两个同名联系人选哪个）时，也会问你。 - 定时任务等你不在场的任务，在询问模式下遇到要花钱的一步不会等人，会直接不做，并照实告诉你哪一步没做成；别的照常做完。 ## 数据与隐私 - **没有 Mika 的服务器。** 你的话、屏幕内容、截图只发给你自己配置的模型服务商。 - API Key、记忆和用户画像用安卓密钥库加密，保存在手机上。对话、运行记录、Token 用量都只存在本机。 - 检查更新只访问 GitHub。 - 内置浏览器访问的是你让它去的网站；沙箱默认断网。 ## 免责声明 - 用自动化方式操作第三方 App 和网站，可能违反它们的用户协议，有被限制功能、封号的风险。请自行判断、自担风险。 - 你同意的动作（以及自主模式下 Mika 替你做的动作）由你负责。重要的事请用询问模式，并检查结果。 - 这是 Beta 软件，按「原样」提供，不做任何担保（详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)）。 ## 常见问题 **无线调试自己关掉了？** 安卓原版在 Wi-Fi 断开、手机重启后会关掉无线调试。设置里的「恢复与修复」中「自动打开无线调试」默认开着：需要时 Mika 会自己打开它再连接（要你允许 Mika 修改系统设置）。第一次在某个 Wi-Fi 上，系统会问是否允许，请手动打开一次并勾选「始终允许使用此网络」。如果还是连不上，回到设置里的「设置手机操作」向导重新配对即可。 **无障碍服务被关掉了？** 系统有时会停掉无障碍服务（比如进程被清理后）。「替我打开无障碍」默认开着，Mika 会自己把它重新打开；修不好时设置页会提示你手动打开。 **有的 App 页面读不到、截不到？** 有些页面（比如付款、输密码）禁止截屏，Mika 看不到画面，也不会去识别上面的字。这类页面需要你接管处理，处理好交还给 Mika。 **为什么推荐安卓 14？旧系统能用吗？** Mika 在一块单独的后台屏上操作 App，安卓 12 起可以使用手机操作能力；安卓 12、13 上操作后台屏可能影响主屏焦点。安卓 14 起后台屏有自己的焦点，不会影响你在主屏打字，所以更推荐。只用网页、沙箱和聊天，安卓 11 也能用。 **能用自己电脑或局域网里跑的模型吗？** 可以。添加服务商时选「自定义」，接口地址填 `http://` 开头的也行，比如 `http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1`（手机和那台电脑在同一个 Wi-Fi 下）。本机和局域网的地址不加提示；不加密又不在局域网里的地址会提醒一句：API Key 和对话内容可能被同一网络里的人看到，能用 `https://` 就用。 **APK 更新从哪来？** 只从本仓库的 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases) 发布。每个版本改了什么，都写在那个版本的发布说明里。 ## 参与贡献 ### 补充 App / 网站知识（不用写代码） 最简单的贡献：给某个 App 写一份 `APP.md`、给某个网站写一份 `SITE.md`，或者改进已有的。它们是带头部的 Markdown 纯文本，放在 `core/src/main/resources/knowledge/` 下。格式见 [`docs/knowledge-format.md`](docs/knowledge-format.md)。 ### 报告问题 开 Issue 时请写上：**手机型号、安卓版本、Mika 版本**（设置里的「关于 Mika」），做了什么、期望什么、实际发生了什么。能附上「查看过程」里的截图更好（注意先遮掉隐私）。 ### 贡献代码 欢迎 PR。先读 [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md)（按代码现状写，带类名和文件路径）和 [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md)（已完成、接下来、已知问题）。改动请带单元测试。 ## 开发者 ### 构建与测试 CLI 测试另需 Python 3.10+,可用 `-PmikaPython=/path/to/python3` 指定解释器。 需要 JDK 17 和 Android SDK（`local.properties` 里的 `sdk.dir`，或环境变量 `ANDROID_HOME`）。 ```bash ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug # 调试包 ./gradlew :app:assemblePerf # 看流畅度用的包：和发布版一样预先编译、不可调试，用调试签名，可直接覆盖调试包 ./gradlew :core:test :core:cliTest :app:testDebugUnitTest # 单元测试 ``` 调试包不做预先编译，界面会慢好几倍；判断流畅度请用 perf 包。 - 仓库有两个模块：`:core` 是纯 Kotlin，主循环、工具、提示词、知识都在这里，可以在电脑上用单测和假模型跑；`:app` 是安卓宿主。 - 沙箱的原生程序和自带运行环境已在仓库里；重新构建见 [`tools/sandbox/README.md`](tools/sandbox/README.md)。 - 真机评测见 [`eval/README.md`](eval/README.md)。 ### 模型配置细节 - 三个用途：**主模型**（办事，要支持工具调用）、**看图模型**（描述界面、看图定位；新装默认不用，可选「用主模型」）、**轻量模型**（判断结局、提取记忆、理解意图等小事，默认用主模型）。 - 「测试并保存」先调一次服务商公开的列模型接口，再带一个试用的工具，请会当主模型的那个模型调用它（用掉几十个 token）；都成了才保存，哪一步不成当场说原因（服务端的报错原样显示）。先试哪个：这家自己的模型在前（例如通义千问先试名字里有 qwen 的），再是列表明说能调用工具的，向量、重排、语音、画图这类不试。试的模型是它自己的问题（这个账号没开通或没权限、没有这个模型、不会调用工具）时接着试下一个，至多 3 个：通过的当主模型，并说一句先试的哪个没通过；都没通过也保存服务商（Key 是对的），不定主模型，说明原因、请你从列表里选一个开通了的，选的时候先试调用。Key、网络、地址不对照旧不保存。没列出模型时（可能这家不提供列表，也可能地址或接口类型填错了），先填一个模型名，再测试就用它试调用，通了才保存；找不到这个模型时说清是哪个、模型名大概长什么样。自定义填的是某家的官方地址时，提醒改用那家的预设（一点就换，Key 留着）。不提供列表的服务商，在选用途时手填的模型名同样先试调用；以前没试过的，服务商那一行提醒「没测试通过」，点进去可以「重新测试」。 - 模型列表上的能力标签（工具调用、看图、上下文长度）：接口给了的照实显示，没给的沿用预设初值并标「未确认」，只作参考，不拦。 - 「看图定位已验证」在设置里的「开发者选项」（调试版可见），对当前看图模型生效。 ### 文档 - [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md)：整体结构。 - [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md)：已完成、接下来、已知问题与暂缓。 - [`docs/knowledge-format.md`](docs/knowledge-format.md)：App、网站知识与技能的格式。 - [`docs/sandbox/skill-scripts.md`](docs/sandbox/skill-scripts.md)：知识与技能自带的沙箱脚本。 ### 发布与更新（维护者） - 发布在 GitHub Releases，tag 用 `vX.Y.Z`，APK 作为附件挂在这个版本上。 - 检查更新：每次打开 App 查一次 `https://api.github.com/repos/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest`，不经别的地址。 - 关于页点「下载更新」后由系统下载服务在后台下载 APK，可查看进度、删除下载或失败后重试，重开应用仍可继续查看。下载完成后点「安装更新」，首次按提示允许 Mika 安装未知应用，再在系统安装页确认。安装前检查 APK 大小、发布附件提供的 SHA-256、包名、版本号和签名证书，系统安装器还会再验一次签名；自行编译、签名不同的版本不能直接覆盖成官方版，要先卸载。发布未包含 APK 时仍打开发布页。 ## Star 增长 ## 联系作者 - X：[@wangzan101](https://x.com/wangzan101) - 微信群：在 App 设置的「关于 Mika」›「加入交流群」扫码。 - X 群聊： ## 许可证 Mika 以 [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) 发布，版权声明见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。 第三方组件保留各自的许可证，见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。其中：APK 里带有 PRoot（GPL-2.0-or-later，静态链接 talloc，LGPL-3.0-or-later）编译成的独立可执行程序 `libproot.so`、`libproot_loader.so`，Mika 只以子进程方式运行它们；源码地址与校验值在 [`tools/sandbox/sources.lock`](tools/sandbox/sources.lock)，补丁在 `tools/sandbox/patches/`，可以用 `tools/sandbox/build-native.sh` 重新编译。沙箱的运行环境（Alpine Linux 3.22 的最小根文件系统和软件包）随 APK 发布，发布时附带对应源码包，做法见 [`tools/sandbox/README.md`](tools/sandbox/README.md)。
